## What it is

The drip tray of the scale, in the Profitec GO's base plate. A watertight PETG tub, one solid, modelled in the machine frame (X from the base plate's left inner wall, Y from the machine face toward the user, Z from the top of the base plate floor) and returned through `scale_frame`. It hangs from the plate's side walls by two shoulders, runs 23 mm into the mouth at the back and locks behind the front lip. Over the scale (X 72 and east) a plateau at Z 20 comes down a 45° ramp to the well; west of it, where nothing stands under the tray, the floor climbs gently from the well toward the mouth. The rear is not a wall but a 45° slope over the full width: the purge water falls on it and runs forward. A Ø42 lens-shaped window with an 8 mm kerb lets the tower through to the load cell; the TPU chimney (`scale_chimney`) pushes over the kerb. Rails along both side walls carry the outer grille with the front wall top. Two pegs grow out of the slope toward the mouth: the west one meets the machine's bumper, the east one carries the TPU `scale_bumper`. It prints standing on its front wall (`scale_tray_standing`). Bambu PETG Basic, printed on the P2S.

## Design notes

Every mating dimension comes from `scale_layout().tray`; the base plate and mouth from `measurements.toml`. Body X 9.5 to 183.5, Y -23 to 139.5, walls and floors 2.5 (each zone is one section offset inward by one wall, so floor and wall must be equal: `reject` otherwise).

- Print stance: standing on the front wall's outer face (Y 139.5), growing toward the mouth, so for printing "down" is +Y. Every face was drawn against that: the floor's underside, the side walls, the shoulders, the corbels, the rails and the pegs have no +Y component; the plateau's ramp underside and the rear slope's inner face are exactly 45°. No supports, no facet, no fins.
- Plateau (X 72 to 183.5): underside at 20.0, from the rear to Y 89, then a 45° ramp down to Z 2 at Y 112, then flat to the front wall.
- **How low the plateau can go** (2026-11-17): its underside must stay 1.3 mm (`SCALE_CLEARANCE`) over the highest part of the scale under it, which `_refuse_misfit` checks against all three (`_scale_tops`). Tops: the base's bridge beam 18.7 (cell top 15.7 + 0.6 gap + 2.4 beam), the adapter 18.7, the PCB box lid 18.6. The plateau sits at that floor, 20.0. Going lower means thinning the beam and the adapter together (the adapter's 3 mm over the cell is set by its magnet wells), then the lid (19.9). Lowering the plateau moves the chimney's bottom with the plateau's floor; the kerb's top stays at 35.5.
- West zone (X 9.5 to 72): underside at 2.0 from the front wall back to Y 112, then one straight slope (6.1°) up toward 13.5 at Y 4. The rear slope cuts it first, at Y 9.0 (underside 13.0), so the 13.5 flat never appears.
- Divider: a 2.5 wall in the YZ plane, X 69.5 to 72, from the west floor up to the plateau's floor, wherever the plateau is higher (Y up to 112). It sits west of `plateau_x0` so the plateau keeps its full width.
- Rear slope: one 45° plane over the whole width, 2.5 thick measured square to it; its inner face reaches the rim (48.5) at Y -23. It meets the plateau's floor at Y 3.0 (26 mm before the rear) and the west floor at Y 10.2 (33 mm before). Its underside over the rear lip (Y -2 to 0) is at Z 24.0 to 22.0, and 18.0 over the screw heads at Y 4: at least 10 mm over the 12 mm lip (`reject` under 13).
- Window and kerb: `scale_lens` outlines, Ø42 with 2 mm tips, kerb 2 thick from the plateau's floor (22.5) to 35.5. The kerb spans X 74 to 120, Y 23.1 to 84.9; the chimney's 1.6 sleeve over it reaches X 72.4 and Y 86.5, both on the flat of the plateau (X from 72, Y -2 to 89; `reject` otherwise). Standing, the -Y tip roofs the window (no hole ceiling) and the +Y tip is where the kerb starts on the floor.
- Front wall: Y 137 to 139.5, from the well's underside (Z 2, 15 below the front lip's top) up to the rails' level, 46.0. Its outer top edge is square: a bevel there ends on the bed face (see Don't). The outer grille bears on the full 2.5 of its top: 421 mm².
- Rails: 3.0 wide, 2.5 thick, top at 46.0, along both side walls only, on a 45° corbel down to 40.5. They run from the front wall back to where the rear slope cuts them (Y -20.5 at their top). Contact with the outer grille, measured: 424 mm² each.
- Shoulders: 2 mm flange, Z 47 to 49, Y 2 to 139.5, out to X -4.5 / 197.5 (2.5 beyond the plate walls' outer faces); square-ended, their front end on the bed. The flange's top stands 0.5 above the rim (48.5), too little for a 1 mm chamfer, so that edge stays sharp.
- Locating corbels under each flange, Y 40 to 139.5 (front end on the bed): a 3 mm vertical face at X 0.5 (192.5 on the east), so 0.5 mm of play to each wall's inner face, then 45° back to the body wall at Z 35.
- Rear pegs, Ø10 along -Y, solid where they cross the slope (the part that would reach into the tub is cut away with the cavity). West at (49.5, Z 32), end at Y -23: 1 mm in front of the machine's bumper tip (-24). East at (157.5, Z 32), end at Y -29.5, for the TPU cap (end of cap at -31, 1 mm from the back of the mouth). Each leaves the slope between Y -5 (its lowest line) and -15 (its highest) and has a 2.5 structural 45° fill at the root. Standing, each is a vertical pin at most 14.5 mm free above the slope's highest point of contact; nurb's `pin` rule stays silent.
- Water, computed from the model up to Z 43.5 (the rails' underside), minus the rails and the kerb's column (the window inside it is sealed by the chimney): 597 cm³ (0.60 L) in all, 283 west of X 72 and 315 over and around the plateau; 165 of it is the front well (Y 112 to 137, both zones). The chimney's sleeve takes about 4 cm³ more. Version 1 held 0.69 L to 5 mm below its brim.
- Part volume 149 cm³ (polished), about 190 g of PETG at 100 % fill.
- Guards (`reject`, from the layout): floor and wall unequal, rim more than 49.0 (mouth ceiling 51 minus 2), plateau underside under 20.0 (highest part of the scale under it plus 1.3), well underside not below the front lip (17), plateau starting less than 3 mm west of the scale (X 76) or its ramp less than 3 mm in front of it (Y 76), body wider than the mouth, rear end past the left bumper (Y -24), west underside under 13 over the rear lip and screw heads, kerb or sleeve off the plateau's flat.
- Polish: 1 mm on straight convex edges, skipping the faces other parts bear on (shoulder undersides, locating faces, rail and front wall tops, the side walls' inner top edges that guide the grille in), the kerb and window, every edge in the bed face, every edge whose chamfer would face more than 45° toward +Y, and acute edges (the rear rim, where a chamfer leaves a sliver thinner than the knife it blunts). 36 of the 37 edges take it; the flange-top edge above does not. No slivers.

### Printing

`scale_tray_standing` is the print: the default turned so the front wall's outer face lies on the bed, mouth end up, 202 x 47 x 169 mm on the P2S's 256 mm bed. First layer: the front wall, the side walls' ends, the shoulders' and corbels' front ends, 7 860 mm², under the warp threshold. Turned 45° about the vertical it would cover 166 x 166 mm (169 tall), so it would also fit the A1 mini's 180 mm bed.

`nurb check` on the variant finds two things, both accepted here:

- overhang, 50 mm² at 90°: the kerb's +Y tip. The lens outline gives the kerb's outer tip a 4 mm radius (window tip 2 plus the 2 mm wall), so standing, the kerb's lowest 5.7 mm of arc faces down; it is the kerb's first strip, 8 mm long, anchored on the floor at one end. Nothing can fill under it: the chimney's sleeve has to slide over the kerb down to the floor. nurb has no accepted count for overhang, so it stays listed.
- min_wall 0.70 mm: the rear rim's 45° edge (see the fence), accepted with `min_wall = 0.7`.

The default is the assembly pose (it must stay there for `scale_assembly`), not a print pose: printed that way the plateau, the shoulders and the pegs are flat overhangs and float, the window rim is a hole ceiling, and its centre of mass falls off the well floor. Its findings are expected.
- **Web under the kerb's tip.** A web `kerb_web_width` (10 mm) wide carries the 45° ramp up to the top of the kerb's tip on the user's side, so the tip's rounded end grows from the web instead of starting in the air (owner's idea, 2026-11-16). It replaces the one overhang the standing print had left (50 mm2 at 90°). The chimney straddles it through a notch, so the sleeve does not grip the kerb over those 10 mm.

## Don't

- Do not print it upright on supports, nor tilted 45° on a flattened front corner: upright, the plateau's 8 600 mm² underside, the shoulders and the rear rail all needed support; tilted, it stood 143 mm tall on an 8 mm facet with its weight 30 mm behind it, held by adhesion alone, and the facet cut into the well's front corner. Standing on the front wall needs neither.
- Do not put back a vertical rear wall, a rear rail, or any face that looks toward +Y more than 45°: standing, such a face is a flat ceiling. The grille is carried by the side rails and the front wall.
- Do not bevel the front wall's outer top edge: that edge ends on the bed face, and the 1.5 bevel laid a 358 mm² knife edge on the first layer (`bed_bevel`). The outer grille's apron corner is square to match.
- Do not chamfer the rear rim's edge, nor any acute edge: the 1 mm chamfer left a 0.21 mm section.
- Do not raise the pegs' root fill to 3 mm: on the east peg, 2 mm above the plateau's underside, it does not land.
- Do not open the slope behind the pegs: it holds water.
- Do not run the locating corbels behind Y 40: unknown screw heads may stand near the rear of the side walls.
- Do not put anything on the floor around the kerb, even to carry its +Y tip: the chimney's sleeve stands there.
- Do not chamfer the shoulder undersides, the locating faces, the rail tops or the front wall top, nor add a lead-in on the inner top edges of the walls; do not chamfer the kerb, the window or the pegs.
- Do not put back the splash ball: the rear slope catches the purge water now and turns it forward.
- Do not remove the web under the kerb's tip, and do not start it at the kerb's wall: it starts inside the window (cut afterwards) so that it fuses with both flanks; started at the wall it left a 0.08 mm crevice beside them.

## Changelog

- 2026-11-16 — First model, upright in the machine frame: raised zone and full-width well behind a vertical well wall, rails on three sides, shoulders, window and kerb, splash ball, peg on a vertical rear wall. It needed supports to print.
- 2026-11-16 — Tilted print: a `diagonal` variant stood at 45° on an 8 mm facet cut across the front-bottom edge, shoulders cut at 45° in plan, rear rail without corbel. Dropped: 143 mm tall on 8 mm of adhesion, and the facet ate into the well's corner.
- 2026-11-16 — Rebuilt to print standing on the front wall (`standing` variant; the default stays in the frame for the assembly): plateau with a 45° ramp beside a gently sloping west zone and a divider wall; 45° rear slope instead of a rear wall; lens-shaped window and kerb on the plateau's flat; side rails only; square front wall top (no bevel); square shoulder ends; corbels from the front to Y 40; both pegs on the slope with a root fill; splash ball, rear rail, well wall, `diagonal` and `stand_facet` removed.
- 2026-11-16 - Web under the kerb's +Y tip; the standing variant checks clean.
- 2026-11-17 - Plateau underside 25 -> 20, the floor set by the scale under it (beam and adapter at 18.7, plus 1.3): 5 mm more water over the plateau. The guard now checks the beam, the adapter and the lid, not the adapter alone. Kerb 8 -> 13 mm tall over the floor.
